content: Zhang Zhongjing, whose formal name was Zhang Ji, lived during the Eastern Han dynasty from approximately 150 to 219 CE. He is recognized as one of the most prominent physicians in Chinese history, particularly during the later years of the Eastern Han period. Zhang Zhongjing made significant contributions to the field of Traditional Chinese Medicine by establishing foundational principles of medical practice and compiling the medicinal knowledge of his time. Although he is highly regarded in modern Chinese medicine, very little is known about his personal life. Historical accounts suggest that he was born in Nanyang and held an official position in Changsha. The exact dates of his birth, death, and the completion of his works remain uncertain, but it is generally accepted that he lived until around 220 CE. During his lifetime, the region was plagued by political instability, with warlords vying for control of territories. This period of unrest led to widespread outbreaks of febrile diseases, which also affected Zhang's own family. Zhang Zhongjing acquired his medical knowledge by studying under his fellow townsman Zhang Bozu, analyzing earlier medical texts, and collecting prescriptions from various sources. His dedication culminated in the creation of a monumental medical text titled Shanghan Zabing Lun (Treatise on Cold Pathogenic and Miscellaneous Diseases). Unfortunately, this work was lost shortly after its publication due to the chaos of wartime. Despite this, Zhang's contributions to Traditional Chinese Medicine earned him the title of Sage of Chinese Medicine. The content of Shanghan Zabing Lun was later recovered and reorganized into two separate texts: the Shang Han Lun (傷寒論, On Cold Damage) and the Jinkui Yaolue (金櫃要略, Essential Prescriptions of the Golden Coffer). The Shang Han Lun focused on the treatment of epidemic febrile diseases that were prevalent during Zhang's era, while the Jinkui Yaolue served as a comprehensive collection of his clinical experiences and therapeutic principles. Both texts have undergone extensive reconstruction over the centuries and remain highly influential in the practice of Traditional Chinese Medicine. Zhang Zhongjing is widely regarded as the founder of the Cold Damage school of Chinese medicine. His work continues to be revered, and he is considered a seminal figure in the history of Chinese medical science.
